A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SCOPE and contain 23 readable pages, including Appendices A–H. Text and visual inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, results, figures, tables and presentation without material gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM-judge experiments in Sections 3–4, with additional benchmark, baseline, specialized-critic and robustness results in Appendices C–H.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results in Sections 3–4 and Appendices C–H, including measured uncertainty quality, selective risk, coverage and robustness.

M1.justification: Both versions average aligned preference probabilities from two response orders, compute binary entropy, and calibrate the largest threshold satisfying the same linearized-loss constraint. The revised BPE explanation does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate MT-Bench, RewardBench, Chatbot Arena, JudgeBench and PKU-SafeRLHF, retaining general, reasoning-intensive and safety-focused judging coverage. The calibration-noise and cross-benchmark test scenarios also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments: Predictive Probability, Verbalized Confidence, Swap-and-Aggregate, Simulated Annotators and Self-Consistency for uncertainty; Vanilla, Heuristic, Naive and Trust-or-Escalate for selective prediction.

E3.justification: Section 3 and the appendices retain the same tie filtering, 2,000-instance sampling, 50/50 calibration/test splits, judge configurations, metrics and experimental procedures. Shortening the dataset description does not revise any setting.

E4.justification: The calibration-label-noise study in Appendix F, calibration-size ablation in G, cross-benchmark transfer study in H, and model/risk-level analyses are unchanged. No analysis or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain 1,000 random splits for the main and extended evaluations, 500 splits for Appendices F–H, and the same reproducibility statement. Standard-deviation bands and tabulated uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–12 and the result plots retain their numerical entries and findings. For example, Table 3 reports identical SCOPE coverage/risk of 0.246/0.097 for Qwen-7B on MT-Bench at alpha = 0.10.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, equations, Theorem 2.1 and Appendix A proof are unchanged. The entropy maximum at averaged probability 0.5 was already specified in v3's Figure 1 caption and Appendix B.1; v4 refines its explanation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and substantive conclusion retain the same SCOPE risk-control and BPE uncertainty claims. Deleting the conclusion's final two broad sentences about accountable evaluation does not alter the contribution's meaning or scope.

C2.justification: v3 associates maximal BPE entropy with inconsistent predictions across response orders. Section 2.2 and Figure 1 in v4 explicitly include ambivalence and explain that BPE penalizes position bias through the averaged preference without measuring bias directly. This refines the mechanism interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix B preserves the prompts, logit extraction, temperature, baseline configurations, hardware and reproducibility information. Section 3 removes a repeated mention of two forward passes, but this requirement remains documented elsewhere. Access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and substantive research positioning in Section 5 are unchanged. No prior work is added, removed or reassessed.

P1.justification: Section 2.2 and the Figure 1 caption receive local rewrites, Section 3 removes redundant phrases, and Section 7 loses two closing sentences. The section organization and appendix text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 improves the placement of overbars in its averaged-probability notation and revises its caption. Local text reflow shifts main-text page breaks; result tables, plots and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Section 2.2 and Figure 1 clarify that high BPE entropy can reflect ambivalence as well as order disagreement, reducing the misleading impression that BPE directly measures position bias. This clarification and the small notation/prose cleanups improve explanatory precision. The methods, proofs and empirical support remain unchanged.
